name: LeRobot ACT (pusht_image)
notes: ACT (Action Chunking Transformer, ResNet-18 backbone) trains end to end on the public lerobot/pusht_image dataset with zero lines of upstream source changed. Truncated to 300 of the 100000 default steps — a pipeline-viability run, not a converged policy. Two things bite anyone reproducing a framework rather than a script. First, the documented entry point only exists after `pip install -e .`, and an editable self-install makes the tracer treat the whole repository as package territory, so the lineage loses every data and checkpoint edge; the fix is to install the dependency extra, uninstall the package, and import from the checkout. Second — and this is the one that would have shipped an un-rebuildable row — `pip uninstall` leaves `src/lerobot.egg-info/` behind, and because the reproduction puts `src/` on sys.path, `importlib.metadata` reads it straight back as an installed `lerobot 0.6.2`, a version that has never been published on PyPI. Every structural check still passes; only trying to install the recorded environment finds it. Separately, upstream's own wandb logging cannot be bridged to any substitute tracker: `WandBLogger.__init__` calls `wandb.run.get_url()` unguarded, which no wandb-compatible tracker implements, so the run is logged via a dedicated evaluation step instead (held-out eval_loss 0.536 over 2742 frames, matching training's own step-300 number).
